rows: Duplicate JSON keys are collapsed and only the last matching key is retained.
The cmdlet is not a duplicate-key-rejecting schema validator.
PSCustomObject property lookup is case-insensitive and case-variant keys can collapse.
Queue identity fields need a strict canonical-key policy.
GetFullPath converts a path to an absolute path representation.
It does not by itself prove final-handle or reparse-point containment.
The API retrieves the final normalized path for an opened file or directory handle.
A handle must first be opened under the intended reparse policy.
Windows exposes reparse-point detection and open-reparse-point behavior.
String-prefix checks alone do not establish resolved containment.
Moving across volumes becomes copy then delete and some replacement strategies are not atomic.
Generation swaps require same-volume and crash-consistency proof.
File.Replace replaces one file with another and can retain a backup.
Directory generations still need a pointer/manifest transaction.
Flush(true) can flush buffered file data through intermediate buffers.
Directory-entry durability and schema validation remain separate.
update-ref can verify expected old object IDs and group reference updates in a transaction.
File-level worktree CAS is not equivalent to authoritative remote-ref CAS.
git push supports atomic ref updates when the server supports --atomic and supports explicit lease expectations.
Multi-file state still requires one commit/manifest and expected remote head.
Linked worktrees have administrative metadata and support lock, prune, remove and repair operations.
Portable worktrees require identity, containment and lifecycle receipts.
hash-object computes the repository object ID for file or stdin bytes.
Text conversion before hashing changes the blob identity.
Git blob content is treated as an uninterpreted sequence of bytes.
PowerShell text capture is not a binary-preserving blob transport.
ls-tree lists tree entries and their object names and supports explicit output formats.
Parsers should not assume one fixed object-ID width.
Git documents SHA-256 repositories and object-format configuration.
Hard-coded 40-hex SHA-1 parsing is not format-agile.
Repository configuration controls object format, remotes, hooks and worktree behavior.
The effective trusted configuration must be recorded.
Porcelain status is intended for scripting worktree and index state.
A clean worktree does not alone prove an empty isolated index generation.
git diff can compare worktree, index and tree states.
Both pre-stage index and post-stage tree need explicit comparison.
Git provides validation rules for reference names.
Task-derived refs and namespaces should be validated before use.
A commit records the exact staged tree and metadata.
Claim, queue and receipts should be bound to the resulting commit before push.
The current INSPIRE package was published on 5 July 2026 and is replaced on the first Sunday monthly.
Catalogue availability does not prove the downloaded GML bytes.
HMLR supplies GML captured against British National Grid and warns reprojection can shift features.
Exact native geometry and identity receipts remain required.
The official DTM is 1 m, EPSG:27700, metres ODN and ±0.15 m RMSE.
Metadata does not prove fresh WCS response bytes.
Terrain 50 grid supply uses 200 by 200 cells, 50 m spacing and 10 km tiles.
Exact current archive and sidecar hashes remain required.
